focus: Barter-side reality: barter-overlays manifest, replay/sync forks, state, hooks
noveltyJustification: All 9 findings were new to this lineage; the Barter checkout had not been read before iteration 2 and the fork relationship changes the recommended direction.
answeredQuestions: Q2: What do Barter's `barter-overlays` runbook, `overlay-manifest.json`, `replay.cjs`, `sync.cjs` and `sync-state.json` do that the Skilled engine does not, and what is the concrete migration path onto the engine's manifest and state schema?

keyFindings.text: Barter's `replay.cjs` and `sync.cjs` are a fork of the Skilled overlay engine rather than an independent tool: the WHY preamble is the same text about a vendored tree being replaced wholesale, and the shared function names (`planOverlay`, `assertSafeToPlan`, `classifyDestination`, `commandGuard`) match the engine's, so adoption is an upstreaming problem, not a replatform. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/replay.cjs:4] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/sync.cjs:106]

Barter's fork adds a sixth destination state, `fork-drifted`, fed by `upstreamSource` metadata that two entries carry, so a Barter fork of an upstream file stays visible and non-blocking; the engine's `STATUS_NAMES` has five states and never reads `upstreamSource`, so both forks become invisible after migration. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/sync.cjs:17] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/sync.cjs:402] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:67]

The token-name refusal differs in exactly the way that breaks `barter-design-tokens.md`: Barter's fork allows `.md`, `.css`, `.ts` and `.svelte` names, while the engine refuses any basename containing `token` that is not named exactly by the manifest. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/sync.cjs:91] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:1555]

No Barter entry declares `protectedPaths` (0 of 130), so the migration fix for that file is manifest-side: `references/barter-design-tokens.md` added to the `repo-frontend` directory entry's `protectedPaths`, which the engine accepts because it resolves the value relative to the entry. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/overlay-manifest.json:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:1595]

Barter's `sk-git` skill-root entry declares 16 `outsideCertificate` paths with a reason each, and its fork validates and honors them as intentionally vendor-owned; the engine has no reader for `outsideCertificate`, so every exemption those paths carry is lost on migration. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/replay.cjs:813] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/overlay-manifest.json:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:2337]

Barter's `sync-state.json` is already the engine's state shape (`schemaVersion: 1`, `pin`, `files` with 454 destination hashes), so it can seed an engine state file directly, but the engine will only look for that file inside the folder named by `.skilled-overlays.json` (or the literal `skilled-overlays`), and Barter ships neither the setting nor a `skilled-overlays` folder. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/sync-state.json:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:375] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:430]

Barter has no re-pin command at all: neither script mentions `repin`, and the re-pin is an eight-step hand runbook that copies seven runtime folders including `.dsh`, excludes `.opencode/scripts`, then regenerates dsh skill links, runtime mirrors, hook registrations, the trigger index and the advisor graph, and finally compares a Barter fork of the git skill. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/README.md:90] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/README.md:108] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:2914]

Barter's edit guard is a different core from Skilled's `overlay-guard`: it spawns `sync.cjs` from the overlay folder and layers a separate session gate, while Skilled's guard allows immediately unless `.skilled-overlays.json` or `skilled-overlays/` exists at the tree root, so today it is inert in Barter and after adoption two guards would run over the same writes. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/.skilled/hooks/overlay-sync/lib/overlay-sync-core.cjs:11] [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/overlay-guard/lib/overlay-guard.cjs:32] [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/overlay-guard/lib/overlay-guard.cjs:111]

Barter's own documentation has already drifted from its manifest: the vendored `README.md` still pins `23b4f3d2e7` while `overlay-manifest.json` and `sync-state.json` both carry `230d22ba88`, which is the same silent-drift class the engine's own status check cannot see because it never reads a README. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/README.md:9] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/overlay-manifest.json:1]
